counterfactual_missing_items: solid components expected in ovarian fibroma are explicitly absent
no ascites or pleural effusion described to support fibroma-associated Meigs syndrome
imaging phenotype is cystic and fluid-filled rather than solid
decisive_items: a large, fluid-filled lesion measuring 19.3 × 6.2 × 21 cm, located in the pelvis and mid-abdomen, displacing the uterus and compressing the aorta and inferior vena cava
The lesion appeared unilocular with a 1.5 mm wall and no septations or solid components, and was suggestive of an ovarian origin
Transvaginal ultrasound demonstrated an 18 cm diameter ovarian tumor
response.rationale: R2 is strongly supported by a large, thin-walled, unilocular, fluid-filled ovarian cystic lesion with no solid components, matching ovarian cystadenoma. R4 is contradicted by the same raw imaging spans because ovarian fibroma is a solid neoplasm; the explicit absence of solid components and the fluid-filled unilocular morphology make R4 implausible. R4 also relies on non-raw generator opinion rather than a supplied raw support span showing a solid ovarian mass.

rejected.why: Ovarian fibroma is a solid ovarian tumor, whereas the supplied raw imaging spans describe a fluid-filled, unilocular cyst with a thin wall and no solid components, directly contradicting the expected anatomy of a fibroma.
